subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram group messages never dispatched despite confirmed Bot API delivery (DMs unaffected)

question: For Telegram wildcard group configs with no `allowFrom` or `groupAllowFrom`, should maintainers preserve the current explicit sender-authorization requirement and improve diagnostics/docs, or should wildcard `groups` imply sender-open group access?
rationale: The current source behavior is security-sensitive and intentional-looking, while the user-visible setup path can still lead to silent-looking message loss; automation cannot choose the permanent authorization policy safely.

options.title: Keep Explicit Sender Auth
options.body: Preserve `groupPolicy: allowlist` semantics, clarify setup/docs/doctor/gateway status for missing group sender allowlists, and ask reporters to retest with `allowFrom` or `groupAllowFrom` configured.

options.title: Make Wildcard Groups Sender-Open
options.body: Treat `groups: { "*": ... }` as broad group sender authorization, accepting the security and upgrade implications with explicit tests and docs.

options.title: Close As Misconfiguration
options.body: Close this issue as unsupported config and rely on existing doctor/docs warnings, leaving runtime behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Sender Auth
recommendation.body: Preserve `groupPolicy: allowlist` semantics, clarify setup/docs/doctor/gateway status for missing group sender allowlists, and ask reporters to retest with `allowFrom` or `groupAllowFrom` configured.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is a recent contributor on the Telegram ingress/spool path and a plausible owner for coordinating the runtime proof versus policy decision.
